_comment: Every `line` is copied verbatim from a tracked file in this repo; `source` records where.
`tracked` is a synthetic tracked-file set, NOT live `git ls-files`, so an unrelated docs
rename cannot silently break the selftest.
`expect` lists the references the extractor must produce, in order, each with the
resolution rule that must accept it: exact | relative | docs, or null when unresolved.
Written before the regex, per the label-corpus-first rule in persistent-rules.md.
`allowlistCases` covers the other half of the checker: whether an allowlist entry still
earns its place. Each case pairs a synthetic allowlist with the set of references a scan
left unresolved, and states which entries should come back as no longer cited.
Both directions are measured, because a rule that only ever reports failures and a rule
that only ever reports success are indistinguishable from a single passing case.

cases.why: positive: internal spec under notes/, cited as a repo-root path, never tracked
positive: a lost document cited with no directory segment at all, so the extractor must not require a slash
positive: build-time generated NOTICE written one level above the citing workflow, unresolvable from any rule
cases.line: run: cargo about generate -m Cargo.toml about.hbs > ../NOTICE-rust.md

cases.why: positive: a table row naming artefacts of a sibling repository outside kuma; docs-relative must not rescue it
positive: same table, the row the strategy code actually cites as its evidence
positive trap: docs pages named by filename only in changelog prose. docs/en/faq.md and docs/ko/faq.md are tracked, yet neither faq.md nor docs/faq.md is, so every one of these stays unresolved
cases.line: - `~/.kuro/` corrected to `~/.kuma/kuro/` across `docs/en/` and `docs/ko/`, 22 occurrences in 14 files: `configuration.md`, `contributing.md`, `custom-polymerase-editor.md`, `faq.md`, `troubleshooting.md`, `uniprot-and-alphafold.md`, `workspace-save-load.md`.

cases.why: positive trap: a zip member name inside a test literal. The extractor cannot tell it from a citation, so the allowlist is what absorbs it
positive trap: a Korean filename truncates to its ASCII tail, so the extracted reference is a fragment rather than the real name

negative: ../README.md from docs/README.md walks up to the tracked root README
cases.line: Both tabs share a project workspace; a hidden `__kuma_meta__` sheet in every Kuro xlsx export lets Mame auto-match sequencing reads back to the originating project weeks later. See the [project README](../README.md) for installation and architecture.

negative: a bare external URL whose path ends in .md must produce no reference at all
negative: two tracked root files on one line, both resolved by exact match
negative: notes/ is gitignored but a handful of files under it are force-added and tracked, so a notes/ citation is not automatically unresolved

allowlistCases.why: negative: nothing is reported while each entry answers for a citation the scan could not resolve. Without this case a rule that always reports every entry would look correct
positive: the last citation to a lost document was removed, so its entry answers for nothing and must be reported
positive: the real case behind the stale category. The citation text still exists but was corrected to a tracked path, so the reference stops appearing among the unresolved and the entry is stranded
positive: more than one stranded entry, reported in sorted order rather than allowlist order so the output is stable across edits
negative: an empty allowlist strands nothing, even when the scan left references unresolved. Those are reported as unaccounted for by the other half of the check, not here
